prompt: In checkout.py, which line decides where the spans go?

choices.text: tracer.start_as_current_span("POST /orders")
choices.why: That creates a span; it says nothing about where it goes.

choices.text: The OTLPSpanExporter's endpoint
choices.why: Right. And it names the Collector, not Google.

choices.text: Resource.create with service.name
choices.why: That says what produced the data.

choices.text: provider.shutdown()
choices.why: That flushes the batch before exit.

prompt: A short script ends and its spans never reach the Collector. Which line is probably missing?

choices.text: trace.set_tracer_provider(provider)
choices.why: Without it no spans would be recorded at all, a different symptom.

choices.text: The service.version attribute
choices.why: A missing attribute does not stop export.

choices.text: provider.shutdown()
choices.why: Right. The last batch leaves only when the provider is shut down.

choices.text: A time.sleep in each span
choices.why: The sleeps stand for work; they are not needed for export.

prompt: Why do the three inner spans share the trace id of `POST /orders`?

choices.text: They were started inside its with block, as its children
choices.why: Right. Nesting makes them one trace.

choices.text: The Collector joins spans that arrive together
choices.why: The ids are set by the SDK before export.

choices.text: They have the same service.name
choices.why: Every span of a service shares that; traces are separate.

choices.text: They ran in less than a second
choices.why: Timing does not join spans.

prompt: In the Collector's debug output, why does `POST /orders` appear last?

choices.text: Spans are sorted alphabetically
choices.why: 'charge' would then come before 'load'.

choices.text: The parent is sent in a second batch
choices.why: All four were in one batch.

choices.text: The log lists spans as they end, and the parent ends last
choices.why: Right. It ends when its last child has ended.

choices.text: It was the slowest span
choices.why: Order is about ending, not duration.

prompt: A span attribute carries a customer's e-mail address. Where is the cheapest place to remove it from every service?

choices.text: In each service's code
choices.why: Correct but repeated per service, and easy to miss one.

choices.text: In an attributes processor in the Collector
choices.why: Right. One change covers every service sending to it.

choices.text: In Cloud Trace, after it is stored
choices.why: By then the personal data is already stored.

choices.text: In the batch processor's timeout
choices.why: Batching changes timing, not content.

prompt: Match each part of a Collector pipeline to what it does.

pairs.right: what happens to it on the way

prompt: To send the shop's spans to Cloud Trace instead of the debug log, what changes?
hint: The code still sends OTLP to localhost.

choices.text: checkout.py's exporter
choices.why: The code is untouched; that is the point.

choices.text: The Collector's exporter, in its file
choices.why: Right. debug becomes googlecloud.

choices.text: The OpenTelemetry SDK version
choices.why: The version is irrelevant to the destination.

choices.text: Every span's attributes
choices.why: Attributes travel unchanged.

prompt: `otelcol-contrib validate` exits 0 on collector-gcp.yaml. What does that prove?

choices.text: That Google accepted a test span
choices.why: Nothing was sent; the Collector was not started.

choices.text: That the service account has cloudtrace.agent
choices.why: No credential was checked.

choices.text: That every component and key is known
choices.why: Right. A misspelt key fails it, as projectt did.

choices.text: That the traces will appear in Cloud Trace within a minute
choices.why: Validation says nothing about delivery.

prompt: A team moves from Cloud Trace to another vendor. What has to be redone?
hint: What is written against Cloud Monitoring?

choices.text: The instrumentation in every service
choices.why: That is what OpenTelemetry keeps portable.

choices.text: Nothing at all
choices.why: The vendor-side work does not move.

choices.text: Dashboards, alert policies and SLOs
choices.why: Right. The instrumentation moves; those stay behind.

choices.text: The semantic conventions of the attributes
choices.why: They are the same everywhere.

prompt: On Cloud Run, how does the googlecloud exporter authenticate?

choices.text: With a key file mounted into the sidecar
choices.why: A key is the last resort and not needed.

choices.text: As the service account, through the metadata server
choices.why: Right. With roles/cloudtrace.agent.

choices.text: With the developer's application default credentials
choices.why: Those live on a laptop.

choices.text: It needs no authentication inside Google
choices.why: Every call is authenticated, as some identity.
